Live research (Oct 2026): The McMaster University Award of Excellence is an entrance award for incoming international fee-paying undergraduates (Business, Engineering, Humanities, Science, Social Sciences), assessed by McMaster's admissions/award administration. The official page (https://future.mcmaster.ca/internationalawards, fetched live and rendered successfully) names no professor: evaluation is on 'Personal Growth and Achievement', 'Community Engagement and Contribution' and 'Self-Reflection', applications go through AwardSpring (https://mcmaster.awardspring.ca/signin), and amounts are 'determined by the Faculty' administratively. The page links only to staff directories (Faculty and Staff Directory, Find an Expert, Meet Our Team) rather than naming any individual. Question routing is the 'Contact us' admissions form (https://future.mcmaster.ca/contact-us/), i.e. recruitment staff rather than academic supervisors. As a first-year entrance scholarship with no research/thesis component, no supervising professor or programme faculty member is tied to the award.

Live research (Oct 2026): Waterloo's International Student Entrance Scholarship is an automatic, no-application award for international fee-paying students admitted to full-time first-year degree studies. The official page (https://uwaterloo.ca/future-students/financing/international-scholarships, fetched live and rendered successfully) states 'International fee-paying students admitted to full-time, first-year degree studies will receive $10,000 for their first-year studies. No application is required.' and 'You don't need to apply. Students who are eligible will be automatically granted the scholarship.' No professor, committee member, lab or department is named anywhere on the page; it links only to administrative offices (Student Awards and Financial Aid via the applicant portal, and the international recruitment team at https://uwaterloo.ca/future-students/contact-us/recruitment-team). Because the scholarship is granted automatically on admission with no selection or supervision step, no supervising professor can be tied to it.

Live research (Oct 2026): The Emile Boutmy scholarship is a Sciences Po tuition-fee exemption awarded through the admissions process for the Undergraduate College and the two-year Master's programmes. The official page (https://www.sciencespo.fr/students/en/fees-funding/bursaries-financial-aid/emile-boutmy-scholarship, fetched live and rendered successfully) names no professor: 'This scholarship is awarded based on merit and according to the type of profile sought for this programme. The allocation of the scholarship is intrinsically linked to the admissions process, and the criteria for excellence are evaluated solely as part of the review of the application.' Applicants simply tick a box in the 'Financial information' section of their application; there is no supervisor, research proposal or host laboratory. Emile Boutmy was the founder of Sciences Po (1872) and the scholarship's namesake, not a current supervising professor. The only contact published is the Student Services Centre form (https://forms.sciencespo.fr/en/contact-centre-services-etudiants), an administrative service desk. Excluded groups explicitly include PhD students, confirming the award carries no supervision relationship.

Live research (Oct 2026): HEC Paris scholarships are merit-based and need-based tuition-fee reductions for taught Master's and MBA admissions. The official page (https://www.hec.edu/en/hec-paris-scholarships, fetched live and rendered successfully) names no professor in connection with any award: each scholarship (HEC Foundation Excellence Scholarship, Eiffel Excellence Scholarship, Future Leaders of Africa, Garzouzi Foundation Scholarship, etc.) is decided by HEC's admissions/foundation process, with applications submitted to the administrative mailboxes scholarships@hec.fr and, for questions, 'the Master's Programs Recruitment Team by email at info-masters@hec.fr' - office addresses, not faculty. Several awards are assigned by external bodies (the Eiffel Excellence Scholarship is 'established by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs', managed via Campus France), and the Garzouzi Foundation validates continuing students itself. Donor names (Nicolas and Michele Garzouzi, the HEC Foundation community of alumni) are benefactors, not supervisors. These are taught, non-thesis programmes, so no supervising professor or research group is tied to the scholarships.
